topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by framing the session's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Pathogen and Damage Recognition Signals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects infections and tissue injury through conserved molecular patterns that differentiate foreign threats from self.

topics.label: Toll-Like Receptors and Spatial Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the genetics, cellular compartmentalization, and downstream signaling pathways of pattern recognition receptors, with particular emphasis on toll-like receptors.

topics.label: Cytoplasmic Receptors and Inflammasome Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe intracellular pathogen-sensing mechanisms and the multiprotein inflammasome complex responsible for processing inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Inflammatory Execution, Cell Trafficking, and Systemic Consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover how sentinel cells trigger the inflammatory cascade, direct leukocyte recruitment and lymphatic drainage, and potentially cause severe systemic pathologies when overactivated.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Containment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation, rebuild damaged tissues, and manage unresolved infections through chronic containment strategies.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the presentation and announces the topic of the subsequent lecture.
